title: LRU Cache
hints: get needs O(1) lookup by key - that alone points to a hash map from key to some node holding the value
but you also need to know, in O(1), which entry is least recently used when you need to evict - a hash map alone can't tell you that ordering
keep a doubly linked list of entries ordered by recency, so the least recently used entry is always at one fixed end and the most recently used is always at the other
have the hash map store key -> pointer to that key's node in the linked list, so any access can jump straight to its node and unlink/relink it in O(1)

every get or put on an existing key: unlink its node and re-insert it at the most-recently-used end; every put on a new key: insert a new node at the most-recently-used end, and if capacity is now exceeded, remove the node at the least-recently-used end (and its hash map entry too)
commonMistakes: forgetting that get also counts as a use and must bump the key's recency, not just put
forgetting that put on an already-present key must update its value and bump recency without changing the cache's size or evicting anything
evicting based on insertion order instead of last-used order, which is wrong once a get has touched an older entry
not removing the evicted key from the hash map when removing its linked list node, leaving stale entries

content.problemStatement:
You're given a fixed `capacity` and a space-delimited sequence of `ops` to
run against an initially empty Least Recently Used (LRU) cache. Each token
is one of:

- `"put_<key>_<value>"` - insert or update the value for `key`, marking it most recently used, evicting the least recently used entry first if this exceeds capacity
- `"get_<key>"` - return the value for `key` if present, marking it most recently used, or `-1` if absent

**Simulate the operations in order and return a list containing the result of every "get" operation, in the order they occurred.**

Accessing a key with either `get` or `put` always counts as using it.
notes: get called on a key that was never put
put on an already-present key updates its value without changing the cache's size or triggering an eviction
capacity of 1, where every put after the first evicts the previous entry
a get on a key bumps its recency, changing which key gets evicted by a later put

sampleTestCases.input: capacity = 2, ops = "put_1_1 put_2_2 get_1 put_3_3 get_2 put_4_4 get_1 get_3 get_4"
sampleTestCases.explanation: get_1 returns 1 and makes 1 most recent; put_3_3 evicts 2 (least recently used); put_4_4 evicts 1

sampleTestCases.input: capacity = 1, ops = "put_1_1 get_1 put_2_2 get_1 get_2"
sampleTestCases.explanation: with capacity 1, put_2_2 immediately evicts the only entry, key 1

sampleTestCases.input: capacity = 2, ops = "put_1_1 put_2_2 put_1_10 get_1 get_2"
sampleTestCases.explanation: put_1_10 updates the existing key 1 to value 10 and marks it most recently used, it does not count as a new insert

optimal.time: O(1) per get or put operation
optimal.pattern: hash map from key to node, combined with a doubly linked list ordered by recency (most recently used at one end, least recently used at the other)

bruteForce.approach: store entries in a plain list of (key, value, last-used-time) tuples; for every get or put, linearly scan to find the key and update a timestamp, and on eviction linearly scan for the minimum timestamp
